title: Maintenance for an unemployed husband - can men actually claim it
p1:
Can an unemployed husband ask his wife for maintenance?

Most people would immediately say no. But the law does not always see financial support through the lens of gender.
p2: A common misconception is that only women can claim maintenance. In reality, if a husband is unable to support himself and meets the required legal conditions, he may have a right to seek financial assistance from his wife.
p3:
The key factor is not whether someone is a man or a woman. Courts generally look at circumstances like earning capacity, financial dependency, ability to work, and the responsibilities of both spouses.

The surprising part? A spouse's obligation can sometimes depend more on economic fairness than traditional roles. An unemployed husband is not automatically entitled to maintenance, but being a man does not automatically disqualify him either.

The practical takeaway: family law is moving beyond assumptions and focusing on facts, needs, and circumstances.

Should maintenance laws be viewed through financial need rather than gender expectations?
